title: Compliance Forms, Certifications, and Bid Submission Execution
capability_statement: Parsons routinely executes the full administrative-compliance package for state and federal procurements: portal-based bid submission, transmittal letters with delegated signature authority, addenda acknowledgments, ownership and investigations disclosures, exceptions/no-exceptions statements, mandatory insurance certifications, supplier-diversity utilization plans, and the supporting attestations (AWS PCI-DSS, SOC 2 Type II, accessibility/ACR, security testing) that state procurements typically require as separate exhibits. On the Maryland MDOT MVA emissions submittal, Parsons filed through eMaryland Marketplace (eMM vendor number 259737), acknowledged Addenda 1-16, designated dual signatories (Senior Vice President + Senior Program Director), and stated 'NO exceptions' to RFP, contract, and exhibit provisions [3621, 3647]. On the PennDOT 3522R12 submittal, Parsons assembled and filed the corresponding compliance set including AWS PCI-DSS Compliance Attestation, SOC 2 Type II Report and Spreadsheet, Section 508 / WCAG Accessibility Conformance Reports, Disaster Recovery Plan, Escrow Agreements, and redacted Security Testing Results as numbered attachments [1960]. The dossier-level posture supporting these filings: Parsons Corporation is a publicly traded NYSE-listed company (NYSE: PSN), recognized 17 consecutive years by Ethisphere as one of the World's Most Ethical Companies, ranked #1 ENR Program Management firm (2025), with a Chief Legal Officer (John Martinez, named December 2025) and CEO Carey Smith holding NACD Fellow / NACD cyber-governance certifications [3554, 3555, 3556] - all material facts that flow directly into Ownership Disclosure, Disclosure of Investigations, and corporate-responsibility forms.

differentiators: Parsons brings a publicly traded NYSE-listed corporate parent (NYSE: PSN) with documented IPO advisory record, a 17-year run of Ethisphere ethics recognition, and an in-house Chief Legal Officer (John Martinez, named Dec 2025) - which materially de-risks the corporate-disclosure, investigations-disclosure, and signature-authority sections of state forms [3554, 3556, 3567]. The Maryland submittal demonstrates 'no-exceptions' bid posture and >30% MBE / 2% VSBE diversity commitments executed in a real state filing with eMM vendor number, dual-signatory transmittal, and 16-addenda acknowledgment [3621, 3647]. The PennDOT submittal demonstrates pre-built compliance-attestation depth: AWS PCI-DSS, SOC 2 Type II, Section 508 / WCAG ACRs, Disaster Recovery, Escrow, and redacted Security Testing Results delivered as discrete numbered attachments rather than narrative-only - a configuration that maps directly onto the New Jersey-style Third-Party Information Security Questionnaire and supplemental security forms in this theme [1960]. Cleared-workforce concentration (multiple acquired companies at 80-90%+ TS/SCI) and CEO-level NACD cyber-governance / PMP credentialing add further weight to corporate-officer attestations [3531, 3554, 3555].
gap_notes: Most requirements in this theme are direct, mechanical submission obligations - portal filing (NJSTART eProcurement), Q&A submission via portal tabs, ownership-disclosure forms, MacBride Principles certifications, Iran investment-activities certifications, Disclosure of Investigations Parts 1-3, exceptions to State Standard Terms and Conditions, dues authorization Exhibits A/B, performance-security submission, and continuing-obligation notification clauses. The provided Parsons evidence does NOT contain the actual completed New Jersey forms (no NJSTART screenshots, no completed Ownership Disclosure for 10%-or-greater owners, no completed MacBride box-check, no completed Iran disclosure, no completed Disclosure of Investigations Parts 1-3, no completed dues/COPE Exhibits A/B, no Cyber Breach Insurance certificate showing $2,000,000 minimum, no Commercial General Liability $1,000,000-per-occurrence COI, no Professional Liability/E&O policy face). Two material disclosure items must be reported on Disclosure of Investigations forms based on the dossier: (1) Parsons protested the New Jersey Bid Solicitation #20DPP00471 (Enhanced Motor Vehicle Inspection Maintenance System) award to Opus Inspection in 2021/2022, and protested the 2016 award - these are public-sector adverse civil/administrative matters within the standard 5-year disclosure window for some forms [3538, 3558]; (2) a Virginia Business reference to a $250M classified contract 'lawsuit' is noted in the dossier, with specifics 'not material here' per the dossier author's framing - capture team must obtain primary source before any sworn certification [3558]. The Confidential State Department contract wind-down and the FAA BNATCS prime-integrator loss are commercial/financial events, not investigations, but may surface in financial-capability narrative (Tab I-style) [3557, 3558]. Insurance: dossier does not state policy limits actually carried; capture must pull current COI to confirm the >=$2M Cyber Breach and >=$1M CGL thresholds. Subcontractor (Tab K) and Legal Action Summary (Tab L) detail must be assembled fresh - none of the 16 dossier chunks list current Parsons-side litigation comprehensively. The FAA BNATCS market-impact disclosure (~15-23% stock drop, analyst downgrades) is not directly responsive to investigations-disclosure questions but capture should review the Ownership Disclosure publicly-traded-company question (R-004) since Parsons is NYSE-listed and most equity-detail disclosures are then waived under typical state form instructions [3554, 3567]. Theme is overwhelmingly direct, mechanical submission - honest framing: Parsons has the institutional muscle and prior-state-submittal evidence to execute the package, but every form must be freshly completed by the capture team with current data; the dossier and prior submittals serve as posture and template, not as drop-in answers.
